changes_from_v2_2: gpu: Colab's G4 runtime, a whole RTX PRO 6000 at 600 W, the main environment from 2026-11-04; the cluster's 300 W limit was a property of its nodes, not of the experiment. Results stay apart from the cluster's and Nebius's until the cross-environment review at the end of the experiments
verify_schedule: the cost table and the 7 STS temperatures measured and fitted again on the G4 by job A, in a file of their own; a schedule holds only for the environment it was measured on
verify_schedule.replay: stop_if_gain_below unchanged; the G4's N_t is unknown until job C measures it
hypotheses.H1.expect: undecided up to C = 16 instead of C = 8, from the G4's cost table, before any dev run; the rule is unchanged
trees.baseline.rule: by a commit, which is how v2.2 was synced

gpu.name: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition

main.rule: a clean clone of one commit; every main line's --commit

baseline.rule: the engine stays at ad87956; this protocol and the measurement tools are synced to it first, by a commit that leaves the engine alone

order: all lines of one (C, seed) run back to back in one job; the i-th seed (0-based) of a panel starts with the (i mod n)-th of that panel's n lines (dev.lines on D48, confirm.versions on K128b) and continues in listed order
kv_budget: C * ceil((max_prompt_len + max_tokens + 7) / 256) target blocks for every line of both trees; a block draft's cache mirrors the target's blocks

warmup.requests: first C of the panel, cycled

decision.a_beats_b: all paired gains same sign and abs(median) > 2*N_t
decision.report: median (min-max), two decimals; range only if max-min > 0.05. The README's headline, total table and figures are the exception: only the median of the 3 seeds, marked as such; the ranges go in RESULTS
decision.revised: 2026-11-02: the README rule of report decided by the author; the verdicts are unchanged

invalid_if: decode step or round > 3 x median
lines of one (C, seed) split across jobs: one job is one directory, protocol and panel, each line at the commit of its own tree

verify_schedule.made_by: job A on a G4 runtime: tools/profile_verify_cost.py, then tools/fit_confidence_sts.py; reviewed by the author before this protocol is frozen

cost_curve.round: one round's phase timings summed, propose through commit_copy, on CUDA events; every row verifies query_len positions through the variable-length path, the confidence copy included; fresh requests of context_len random tokens for every (batch, query_len)
cost_curve.revised: 2026-11-02 from v2.1's external.cost_curve, which timed the verify forward alone: the schedule weighs a whole round

calibration.record: every round, each row's 7 confidence logits and its accepted count; all 8 positions are verified, so 'the first i drafts all accepted' is observed for every i
calibration.method: STS: for i = 1..7 in turn, T_i on the grid minimizing the binary cross-entropy of the survival prod_{j<=i} sigmoid(z_j / T_j) against 'the first i drafts all accepted', T_1..T_{i-1} fixed
report_only: ECE over 10 equal-width bins, per position and pooled, raw and after STS
AUROC of the survival pooled over positions, raw and after STS

replay.rounds: the calibration runs' rounds of C rows
replay.rule: a row with n of its 7 drafts accepted accepts min(n, L - 1) when it verifies L positions; a round's time is the cost table's at its token count, the fixed-length round's at 8 per row
replay.source: 2 x N_t, N_t = 1.26% in the cluster's job 236550, kept until the G4's own is measured

H1.expect: faster at C = 32 and 64, undecided at C <= 16

H2.rule: the smallest C at which H1 finds dspark_var faster on D48
H2.compare: DeepInfer's MoE estimate: -1.5% at 16 requests per GPU, +11% at 96

H3.of: every line against its k0_line; crossover as decision.crossover

report_only: tokens per round, round-weighted and per request
TTFT, ITL and round time p50 / p99
the confidence's ECE and AUROC, raw and after STS
stop_if: any gate fails: no performance numbers; find the cause
verify_schedule.replay predicts a C=64 round throughput gain below stop_if_gain_below: no dev matrix; check the calibration and the cost table first
on the dev matrix at C=64 dspark_var is slower than dspark_k7 for every seed: no confirmation job
an invalid run: its whole (C, seed) rerun once, per invalid_if

G2_multi.appendix_a: the early stop emits A within the bound of the target's 0.70; the global maximum's 0.85 lies outside it

equivalence.reference: repeat 1 of the cluster reproduction, job 236550

G1_wide.revised: 2026-10-23 after the first run: decode alone moves logits by up to 1.5 between B=1 and B=16 on these prompts, so the fixed bound 0.5 was below the reference path's own batch-size noise; the bound is now floor_multiple x the decode-only noise floor measured on the same prompts in the same job (the rule G1-aux had)

varlen.rule: one batch of the 8 prompts per rotation of the lengths, so each prompt verifies each length once, with the graph's empty row slots and padding tokens; each row's first L positions against the reference's first L decode steps, under the same bound and argmax rule

graph_eager_varlen.rule: the G1_wide varlen batches through the verification graph and eagerly: bit-identical logits

G2_real.revised: 2026-10-23 after the first run: both lines picked the same position, where the target split 0.5/0.5 over two tokens and the draft put all its mass on one; a one-hot q tests only the trivial residual, so q must now be positive on at least min_draft_support tokens
G2_real.revised_again: 2026-10-23 after the second run: both picked positions had a one-hot target p, so every rejection emits the one target token and the output-distribution check passes trivially (gap 0); p must now be positive on at least min_target_support tokens (decision D3)

confirm.cross_tree: at each C the two k0 lines are compared seed by seed; only when every |Q_steady(k0) / Q_steady(k0_base) - 1| <= 2*N_t do the baseline's R and the main lines' R go in one table, otherwise each line reports its R against its own k0_line only
